video_title: Lakers vs Jazz | Postgame Interviews x Highlights: November 18, 2026

quotes.speaker: JJ Redick
quotes.summary_phrase: JJ Redick on the Lakers' poor offensive performance against the Jazz
quotes.excerpt: We had an expected 120 offensive rating, we did not have a 120 offensive rating.
quotes.quote: The reality is we had an expected 120 offensive rating, we did not have a 120 offensive rating. We were 20 of 43 in the paint, 16 of 26 at the rim, 14 of 17 on non-paint twos, and we were 9 for 33 on threes. So, a tough offensive night for us. Turnovers in the second half, certainly we were not good, and that allowed them to get out and run.
quotes.social_post: JJ Redick breaks down the Lakers offensive struggles against the Jazz, noting the team shot just 9 for 33 from three and struggled with turnovers in the second half.

structured.context: JJ Redick discusses the Lakers' poor offensive efficiency and turnover issues in their loss against the Jazz.

quotes.speaker: JJ Redick
quotes.summary_phrase: JJ Redick on the strategic use of the full-court zone press
quotes.excerpt: I feel like throughout the year you're going to need zone.
quotes.quote: I feel like throughout the year you're going to need zone. Sometimes, even in back-to-backs, you play a team like Utah and Quentin Grimes, who wills over there every single time with pace. You try to slow down some of that movement, some of that ghosting, and a lot of possessions you do end up going to five or man-to-man. That's the process. They do a lot of stuff that creates a lot of pace. I thought overall the zone was pretty good.
quotes.social_post: JJ Redick explains the strategic use of the zone defense against Utah, citing the need to slow down the pace and movement created by Quentin Grimes.

structured.context: JJ Redick explains the strategic reasoning behind using a zone defense to slow down Quentin Grimes and the Jazz offense.

quotes.speaker: JJ Redick
quotes.summary_phrase: JJ Redick on the heavy offensive workload for Luka Doncic
quotes.excerpt: The shot creation that is required from him takes its toll.
quotes.quote: The shot creation that is required from him takes its toll. Having said that, I thought Quentin Grimes did a nice job for most of the game of being aggressive and getting downhill. There are other guys that can do it, but it's part of it when Austin Reaves is out for sure. Just like if Austin Reaves plays against Detroit, if he goes and then plays Monday, we had a great example of that is the game we had last year when we went East. So he has the big night in Toronto, Luka Doncic is out, he's in Slovenia, and then he has the next night, he's solo. We actually had to sit some guys, I think LeBron James sat that night in Boston, goes for 36. We've got 43, 36, and then we go to Philly, Luka Doncic is back, but Austin Reaves is one of those worst shooting nights of the season. You can just see it, it takes its toll.
quotes.social_post: JJ Redick discusses the heavy offensive workload on Luka Doncic and how the physical toll of the NBA schedule impacts player performance when key teammates like Austin Reaves are sidelined.

structured.context: JJ Redick discusses the physical toll of shot creation on Luka Doncic and the impact of player absences on the team's rotation.

quotes.speaker: Walker Kessler
quotes.summary_phrase: Walker Kessler on the team's offensive struggles and need for improvement
quotes.excerpt: It's frustrating. Tonight wasn't our night, but I think our team is going to respond well.
quotes.quote: It's frustrating. Tonight wasn't our night, but I think our team is going to respond well to this loss. With 82 games, when you have a bad game like this, you don't want to spend too much time lingering on the losses. You want to learn from it, move on, because you have to. You have another one Friday. Our offense, as far as not going tonight, we were getting good looks, just wasn't falling necessarily, so I don't think there's cause for concern.
quotes.social_post: Walker Kessler says there is no cause for concern after the loss to the Lakers, noting that the team was getting good looks and just needs to move on to the next game.

structured.context: Walker Kessler reflects on the team's offensive struggles and the need to move on from the loss to the Lakers.

quotes.speaker: Luka Doncic
quotes.summary_phrase: Luka Doncic on the physical toll of the NBA schedule
quotes.excerpt: All NBA team plays 82 games, so that can be an excuse.
quotes.quote: All NBA team plays 82 games, so that can be an excuse. I got to do way better, I know that. I feel like we have some open shots we didn't make, but it's one game, we got to move on.
quotes.social_post: Luka Doncic on the team's loss and the grind of the 82 game schedule: I got to do way better, I know that.

structured.context: Luka Doncic acknowledges his own poor performance and the team's inability to convert open shots against the Jazz.

quotes.speaker: Jake Laravia
quotes.summary_phrase: Jake Laravia on the team's resilience despite a heavy schedule
quotes.excerpt: We're not going to let this loss get to our heads too much.
quotes.quote: We've definitely played a lot of games and it's felt like it, but I think for the most part all the guys, everyone's bodies have been feeling good, everyone's been prepared to go out there on the court and win every night. And again, yeah, like you can't overemphasize this loss because you know we're still in a good spot. We're going to stay connected as a team. We're not going to let this loss get to our heads too much. We got another opportunity Friday to bounce back.
quotes.social_post: Jake Laravia says the team is staying connected and not letting the loss get to their heads, emphasizing that they are still in a good spot.

structured.context: Jake Laravia comments on the team's physical state and resilience following the loss to the Lakers.

quotes.speaker: Quentin Grimes
quotes.summary_phrase: Quentin Grimes on the team's fatigue and short turnaround
quotes.excerpt: We let a lot of emotion last night in last night's game, coming back as a team.
quotes.quote: We let a lot of emotion last night in last night's game, coming back as a team and at the holding and it's a quick less than 24 hours turnaround against a team that's better than their record. I would say and everybody would agree on the team is that and we kind of just uh we try to get as much energy we could into that third and then just just wasn't enough, not enough leg, guys. We all feel like we didn't have none of us played well tonight and we're still in the game, so that's a positive takeaway from for sure from for sure.
quotes.social_post: Quentin Grimes admits the team lacked energy during the quick turnaround against the Jazz, saying we did not have none of us played well tonight.

structured.context: Quentin Grimes discusses the impact of fatigue and a short turnaround on the team's performance against the Lakers.

quotes.speaker: Quentin Grimes
quotes.summary_phrase: Quentin Grimes on JJ Redick's coaching and player development
quotes.excerpt: It's a good problem to have, you know, I mean coach that wants to get you the ball.
quotes.quote: It's a good problem to have, you know, I mean coach that wants to get you the ball, wants to get you in a rhythm and stay in that rhythm that I've been in. So I feel like it's a good thing, you know, I mean he's really good at what he does. We were rolling right now, so I have no no doubt about that he'll be able to keep me in this rhythm that I'm in right now whether once we all get back healthy for sure.
quotes.social_post: Quentin Grimes praises JJ Redick for his coaching and ability to keep players in a rhythm, saying he has no doubt the coach will maintain that flow once the roster is healthy.

structured.context: Quentin Grimes praises JJ Redick's coaching style and his ability to keep players in a rhythm.
